correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the induction on |K|. For H=N_G(<x>)∩K and A={a∈K:<x,a>∈C}, conjugation by H preserves A. An admissible maximal T⊴K in H exists starting with 1. The lift D of (H/T)∩Z(K/T) normalizes U=<x,a,T>: it normalizes <x> and T and centralizes a modulo T. Thus UD/U is a quotient of the abelian group D/T; it lies in C because finite abelian groups are built from cyclic factors, not because C is quotient-closed. Extension closure forces D=T by maximality. A is T-coset-saturated by subgroup closure. Nonidentity hT has a proper centralizer preimage L<K, and induction for L gives |C_{H/T}(hT)| dividing the fixed-point count on A/T. Grouping Burnside's sum by conjugacy classes gives the divisibility of the identity term, then multiplying by |T| restores the target. The argument also handles H/T trivial, K=1, and x outside K. For π-separability one can intersect and splice subnormal π/π′ series; equivalently all composition factors are π or π′ groups, and a chief series gives a normal series in the whole group if that convention is intended. No enumeration, quotient-closure assumption, or formal verification is needed.
